_comment: Shared visual vocabulary for a particle_field scenario, keyed by particle_field_config.scenario_type. The AI tutor has no vision — it only knows the picture from this text, so an element missing here is an element the model will guess about (it invented a battery and resistor before this existed, 2026-08-18). A concept's own `stage` block in ../<id>.json extends this and wins on any conflicting `looks_like`.
viewpoint: The view is INSIDE the metal wire, zoomed in far enough to see individual electrons moving between the atoms. It is NOT a circuit diagram. There is no battery symbol, no resistor symbol, no cell, no switch and no circuit loop drawn anywhere on the screen. The battery is outside the view; the only evidence of it is the field arrows inside the wire and the reading in the meter box.

elements.looks_like: small blue dots with short tails, moving steadily across the screen
elements.means: free electrons drifting through the metal. The tail shows the path each electron just took.

elements.looks_like: grey circles with a plus sign inside, spaced out in a fixed grid, never moving
elements.means: the positive ion cores of the metal lattice — the atoms the wire is made of. Electrons collide with these, and that is what resistance is.

elements.looks_like: orange arrows pointing sideways, one of them labelled E
elements.means: the electric field inside the wire. This is the push the battery creates. It appears when the battery switches on.

elements.looks_like: a dark box in the top left corner showing a formula and a number in amperes
elements.means: the live current meter. The number is the current flowing right now.

elements.looks_like: a short label in the bottom left corner
elements.means: the name of what this state is showing.

elements.looks_like: a few words in a small caption near the top centre
elements.means: the one new thing happening in this state.
